_comment: THE TRADE TABLE — what a project's landmark building looks like.
THIS FILE IS MEANT TO BE EDITED. It is the one piece of Werkstadt that
knows what YOUR projects are about, and the shipped list is only a
starting point. Add a row for the kind of work you actually do and the
town gets a building shaped like it.
How it works: for each project the server reads its index.html <title>,
its meta description, its og:site_name, its JSON-LD name, and the first
60 KB of docs/BRIEF.md and docs/README.md. Each row below is a regular
expression (case-insensitive, JavaScript/Python flavour) and a
schema.org type. The FIRST row that matches wins, so put the specific
words first and the catch-alls last — otherwise `tool` swallows every
project that merely mentions a server.
A hit in the page's own title, og:site_name or JSON-LD name is trusted
on its own. A hit anywhere else (BRIEF, README, meta description) needs
a second, independent hit for the same type before it counts — one stray
word in a README must not decide a whole project's trade.
The `type` must be a schema.org type the world knows how to build. The
ones with their own landmark model are: MusicSchool, Restaurant,
CafeOrCoffeeShop, Hotel, GovernmentOrganization, Carpenter, Plumber,
Manufacturer, EducationalOrganization, HomeAndConstructionBusiness,
Photographer, SoftwareApplication, SoftwareSourceCode, Book,
VideoObject. Anything else falls back to a generic civic building.
Not English? Add your language to the same row rather than making a new
one — the pattern is a normal alternation:
{ "match": "\\brestaurant\\b|\\bimbiss\\b|מסעדה", "type": "Restaurant" }
trades: -- lodging: Deliberately NOT `breakfast` or `booking`: both false-positive on ordinary software projects (a `booking flow` is a widget, not a hotel).
-- civic: Deliberately NOT `district` or `region`: a directory of local businesses is not a municipal site.
-- photo: Two-sided on purpose: `drone` alone is a hobby word, `aerial photography` is a trade.
-- catchall: Last on purpose. Every developer project mentions one of these words somewhere.
